channel.title: Information Security
channel.description: This channel features presentations by leading experts in the field of information security. From application, computer, network and Internet security to access control management, data privacy and other hot topics, you will walk away with practical advice for your strategic and tactical information security initiatives.
channel.brighttalk:strapline: The latest trends and best practice advice from the leading experts

item.title: Identity Before Intelligence: Securing Hybrid and AI-Enabled Networks
item.description:
Hybrid networks connect people, cloud services, remote devices and automated workloads. But the introduction of AI assistants adds another access question: when software acts on a person’s behalf, whose permissions govern the data it uses and the actions it takes? A successful sign-in alone does not address that.
In this vendor-neutral session, consultant and business owner Olufela "Lu" Fagbure will work through an illustrative support workflow to show how teams can map human and workload identities, define resource and action boundaries, and separate drafting from approved execution. The webinar connects access policy to enforcement, administrative controls, review evidence and recovery, with practical attention to legacy systems and lean teams.
Attendees will come away from this session knowing how to: - Document one workflow’s access policy. - Identify where authorization must be enforced. - Set a meaningful approval boundary for AI-assisted actions. - Plan a controlled revocation check. A companion worksheet and a suggested 30-day starting plan help turn those decisions into an owner-led review.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Olufela Fagbure, Founder & Director | IT Custom Solutions LLC

item.title: Blocking Isn't Enough: Collaborative Defense for IT Leaders
item.description:
Malicious traffic doesn't stop at your firewall, it moves through a shared ecosystem of infrastructure, routing paths, and mail systems that every organization depends on. Recent Global Cyber Alliance research shows a single cheap VPS was able to fire off roughly 20,000 phishing emails in two five-minute bursts, cycling through brand impersonations while sitting on public blocklists the entire time, proof that blocking known-bad infrastructure isn't slowing attackers down. A parallel study of 191 postal operators found 81% still exposed to email spoofing because of stalled DMARC enforcement.
Tune into this session from CTO Leslie Daigle as she shares concrete network practices to stop compromised devices and protect your infrastructure from potentially devastating breaches. The scale of today's threats means no single organization can block its way out. Progress depends on collaboration among operators, ISPs, and vendors to disrupt shared infrastructure at its source.
Executives will leave with a short list of things to check this quarter: - Whether their organization's ASNs have signed ROAs. - Whether their domains have reached DMARC p=reject rather than sitting at monitoring-only. - Whether outbound traffic is monitored with the same rigor as inbound. - Where their organization could plug into existing collaborative efforts rather than solving this alone.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Leslie Daigle, Chief Technology Officer & Internet Integrity Program Director | Global Cyber Alliance

item.title: Incident Response: Why Organizations Repeat the Same Critical Mistakes
item.description:
Incident response teams have more tools, automation and intelligence than ever before. In turn, the opportunities to make mistakes are also greater.
Organizations are making the same expensive mistakes over and over again. They ignore warning signs and assume someone else is handling the problem. They trust tools and outside experts too much and rush to contain incidents without identifying the true cause. When it comes to supply chain incidents, they assume that if a breach happens at a vendor or service provider, it’s not an internal problem.
In this talk, Alex Holden looks at the common failures that turn manageable incidents into long-term crises. He shares practical lessons from real-world situations, pinpoints common mistakes to avoid and shares a blueprint to help you handle crises efficiently and successfully.
You’ll learn how to: - Identify and eliminate the most common incident response mistakes. - Pinpoint the true root cause behind each incident. - Accelerate responses while reducing assumptions and improving the quality of decisions.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Alex Holden, CISSP, Chief Information Security Officer | Hold Security LLC

item.title: The Governed Hybrid Workforce: Policy and Controls for Human and AI Agents
item.description:
AI agents are now active participants in enterprise operations. Organizations have to govern a workforce that includes employees, contractors, copilots, automated workflows, and autonomous AI agents. This creates a new governance challenge: defining who is authorized to act, under what authority, within which boundaries, and with clear accountability.
Relying on a human-in-the-loop as the last line of defense is no longer sufficient. Enterprises need structured systems where both human and AI actors operate within defined boundaries, with enforceable controls and transparent accountability.
Oksana Denesiuk presents a governance framework designed for the hybrid workforce. She links organizational policy to delegated authority, identity, technical controls, and evidence. Learn how to govern both human and AI actors with clear role definitions, least-privilege access, approval thresholds and enforceable accountability. Enable AI adoption while maintaining security, operational trust and employee agency.
Key Takeaways - Understand why traditional workforce governance models are insufficient once AI agents begin acting inside enterprise systems. - Apply a practical governance chain linking policy, authority, identity, controls, evidence, and accountability. - Define bounded autonomy for AI agents using role scope, least privilege, approval thresholds, segregation of duties, and human override. - Understand where human review is essential and where automated policy enforcement and technical controls provide stronger protection. - Establish the auditability needed to answer five critical questions: what the agent did, why it acted, what authority it relied on, what systems or data it touched, and who remains accountable for the outcome.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Oksana Denesuik, Board Member for ISSA LA, Senior Product Manager, Solution Consultant – Billing | Kaiser Permanente

item.title: There's No Cybersecurity Mindset: Why Diverse Thinking Strengthens Security
item.description:
Adversaries are accelerating their use of automation and AI, outpacing what legacy SOC architectures can handle. Relying solely on new technology addresses only part of the challenge. Effective cybersecurity demands equal focus on people and policy.
Staying ahead requires building adaptive, analyst-driven teams that integrate human and machine strengths. Individuals facing the same threat interpret risks and priorities differently. Harnessing these varied perspectives improves communication, reduces risk and boosts readiness.
Charles Kolodgy discusses why there is no single ideal cybersecurity mindset. Instead, a spectrum of perspectives shapes how teams assess threats, make decisions, and respond to incidents. Tune in to discover why an environment that harnesses these differences to challenge assumptions and drive better outcomes is crucial for resilient security operations.
Key Takeaways: - Pinpoint the elements of diverse cybersecurity mindsets and show how different perspectives influence priorities, risk assessments, incident response, and business decisions. - Apply practical methods to manage mindset diversity, using techniques for constructive challenge, clear communication, conflict resolution, and team cohesion. - Adopt strategies to align varied mindsets across SOC teams, IT operations, leadership, and users. - Recognize how cognitive diversity and complementary mindsets strengthen defenses against complex, evolving threats. - Evaluate how AI is reshaping cybersecurity thinking and how human-machine collaboration changes perception, decision-making, and response.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Charles Kolodgy, Principal | Security Mindsets LLC

item.title: Awareness Alone Fails: Transform Security Habits Across SaaS Environments
item.description:
Attackers exploit established routines and workflows, making traditional training ineffective. Human error is magnified in hybrid environments. The SaaS footprint keeps expanding, access paths keep shifting, and oversight becomes uneven. This drives up fraud losses, data exposure, operational downtime, and regulatory risk. Ultimately, customer trust, employee confidence and your security team's credibility are on the line.
Leaders need to make the secure path the path of least resistance by embedding clear guidance and guardrails into daily workflows and tools. This session examines how organizations can move past compliance-focused training and implement a human-centered security strategy by identifying risky behaviors, reducing security friction, and building controls that employees naturally embrace.
Fatema Fardan, Cybersecurity Digital Data Lead at a leading international bank, draws on lessons from banking, fraud prevention, and cybersecurity operations to show practical ways to measure behavior change, design effective security nudges and balance user experience with risk in today’s hybrid workplace.
Topics for discussion include: - Pinpoint why awareness programs fall short and map risky behaviors across your environment. - Design controls employees actually use, from adaptive MFA to real-time guidance at critical decision points. - Counter phishing and fraud by integrating training, simulations, and behavioral nudges linked to identity signals. - Track what drives impact: reporting rates, time-to-report, reduction in repeat clicks, control adoption, and measurable ROI. - Establish a cross-functional operating model using pilots, A/B testing and leadership dashboards.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Fatema Fardan, Cybersecurity Digital Data Lead | Leading International Bank

item.title: The Agentic Supply Chain: When AI Attacks, Defends, and Decides
item.description:
By 2027, supply chain attacks will strike beyond software dependencies and third-party access to exploit the AI agents, models, data, tools, and automated decisions connecting entire business ecosystems.
This session from industry thought leader Noah Kenney examines the emerging agentic threat surface, including autonomous adversaries that identify and exploit weaknesses at machine speed, model supply chain compromises that propagate across organizations, and AI-versus-AI incidents in which both attack and defense operate with limited human oversight.
Through forward-looking scenarios, attendees will learn how to: - Identify critical dependencies. - Contain cascading failures. - Establish governance, monitoring, and accountability for autonomous systems.
The result is a more resilient supply chain when AI is both a security control and a source of risk.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Noah M. Kenney, Founder & CEO | Digital 520

item.title: Preparing for the 2027 Threatscape: A New Strategy for Operational Resilience
item.description:
The speed of geopolitical risk continues to increase, not least in the differing approaches to the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Governments are now warning that it is "likely, if not inevitable" that national cyber defenses will at some point be breached.
Among this growing spread of challenges, any new strategy must take account of the current level of operational risk. So ask yourself this question: do you do nothing, or do you move your organizational strategy towards planning for the worst?
Join Steve Yates, Chairman of the Resilience Association and Liveryman of the Worshipful Company of Information Technologists, to explore lessons learned from past events and how you should position your organization to be sufficiently prepared for "business-as-unusual".
Key Takeaways: - Identify 2027 threat landscape challenges. - Review the changing direction of operational risk. - Update operational readiness and response strategy. - Change leadership thinking about operational resilience. - Establish a joined-up way of thinking with internal and external partners.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Steve Yates, Chairman | Resilience Association

item.title: Open Source + AI: Where Attackers Move Next in 2027
item.description:
Supply chain and AI security failures share a common thread. Adversaries identify structural gaps, assess potential impact, and act before defenders can respond. In 2026, this approach drove major incidents across open source, AI tooling, build pipelines, and interconnected vendor environments. However, attackers do not rely on static tactics. Their methods adapt faster than most organizations can adjust their defenses.
Industy thought leader Yesenia Yser moves the conversation from retrospective analysis to forward-looking action. Using threat patterns, attacker behaviors, and governance breakdowns from 2026, she argues for anticipatory defense. The goal? To understand adversary strategy deeply enough to close architectural gaps before attackers exploit them, not after the damage is done.
For 2027, Yesenia will identify the threat vectors set to define risk across open-source software, AI systems, and supply chains. The session will turn the hard lessons of 2026 into actionable foresight. Expect clear guidance on where advanced attackers are likely to strike next, which structural weaknesses enable those moves, and what defensive architectures can close the most critical gaps.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Yesenia Yser, Founder | Yes2Tech- Software Security Engineering Consulting

item.title: Identity Is the New Perimeter: Defend Against the Authentication-First Attack
item.description:
The most dangerous cyberattacks increasingly don’t look like attacks at all. Instead of deploying malware, adversaries are using stolen credentials, hijacked session cookies, OAuth grants, API keys, and authentication tokens to access systems as seemingly legitimate users.
In this session, John Bambenek explores how identity has become the new security perimeter and a primary attack surface. He explains how defenders can detect identity-based threats that traditional endpoint and network controls may miss. Receive practical approaches for improving visibility, detection, and response across cloud and SaaS environments.
item.brighttalk:presenter: John Bambenek, President | Bambenek Consulting

item.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence and AI: Are We Ready?
item.description:
AI is rapidly changing the cyber threat intelligence landscape, and not always in ways we are prepared for. Threat actors are using AI to remove traditional barriers, scale attacks faster, improve targeting, automate research, and make malicious activity more effective.
At the same time, defenders are increasingly relying on AI-powered tools, AI-generated analysis, and solutions that may be poorly secured, poorly understood, or built on questionable data. More of our security products and business systems are also becoming AI-driven, introducing new attack surfaces, dependencies, and opportunities for manipulation.
Adoption is moving faster than governance, security controls, and regulation, creating new risks across the intelligence lifecycle. In this talk, Alex Holden examines how AI is changing attackers, defenders and the technologies we depend on, where the biggest weaknesses are emerging, and asks whether we are truly ready for what comes next.
Key Takeaways: - Understand how AI is changing both cyber-attacks and threat intelligence. - Recognize new risks introduced by AI-driven security tools and business systems. - Learn where human validation, governance and security controls still matter most.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Alex Holden, CISSP, Chief Information Security Officer | Hold Security LLC

item.title: Securing MCP Servers from Agentic AI Attacks
item.description:
Agentic AI is rapidly integrating into enterprise systems through the Model Context Protocol (MCP.) This introduces new and significant risks. Recent assessments reveal that 43% of tested servers are vulnerable to command injection, 82% use file operations susceptible to path traversal, and 33% contain critical vulnerabilities. Once a single server in a chain is compromised, the risk cascades to 72% of connected systems.
Sandeep Tripathi will examine real-world incidents including tool poisoning, rug pulls, indirect prompt injection, and supply chain remote code execution. He will outline a practical defense strategy: establish clear trust boundaries, categorize tools by risk level, require human-in-the-loop approval for state-changing actions, sandbox runtime environments, and enforce strict schema and parameter validation. Sandeep will also introduce an MCP gateway designed for risk scoring, authorization, validation, approvals, and rate and result limits, along with AWS and Azure guardrails supported by continuous monitoring.
Key takeaways: - Quantify MCP risk with hard signals and real attack paths. - Apply tiered policies: automatically approve read operations, and require human-in-the-loop approval for destructive or critical actions. - Contain the blast radius by enforcing isolation and using least-privilege scopes with just-in-time tokens. - Follow five essential rules: trust nothing by default, treat every server as a potential attack surface, authorize and audit each tool, minimize permissions, and require gating or reversal for material actions.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Sandeep Tripathi, IT Solutions Architect- Cloud | Gacade

item.title: Beyond Users and Workloads: The Agentic Shift in Cloud-Native Zero Trust
item.description:
Cloud-native zero trust matured in two waves. First, companies stopped trusting the network and moved the control plane to identity. Then, the same principle extended to workloads through managed identities, scoped role assignments and microsegmentation between services. Both waves worked on the assumption the actor is deterministic, so you can scope it, gate it and make sense of what it did afterwards.
The advent of agentic AI breaks that assumption. The platforms are catching up, and agent identities are now first-class principals that appear in sign-in logs and can be targeted by policy. Least privilege defeats its own purpose when the agent's entire value lies in deciding for itself what it needs. Meanwhile, the authorization decision has quietly migrated out of the policy engine and into the model.
This session traces the shift from securing users and workloads to securing autonomous cloud actors. Viewers will leave with an architectural path grounded in the Cloud Security Alliance Agentic Trust Framework.
Key Takeaways: - How to give agents real identity. - Move authorization back out of the model. - Carry provenance through delegation chains. - Close the gap between overseeing agents with ability to stop them.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Dami Baiyeroju, Principal Architect | RYZA

item.title: From Connectivity to Control: Building Vendor‑Resilient OT
item.description:
Operational technology faces a new reality. Each new integration with vendors, cloud platforms and Industrial IoT ecosystems increases efficiency but also exposes critical operations to third-party risk. One compromised partner can disrupt essential processes and threaten business continuity. Organizations need to find way of getting the benefits of connectivity while maintaining control, even when external parties are compromised.
In this session, Vincent Amanyi (Founder, Boleaum Inc.) shares a framework for designing secure, resilient and vendor-independent OT architectures that maintain operational performance and business agility. Learn how to protect critical industrial assets from third-party vulnerabilities with zero-trust principles, network segmentation, secure remote access controls and governance frameworks.
Receive practical strategies for designing OT architectures that keep control over critical systems, data, and operations—regardless of vendor involvement.
Topics for discussion: - Reduce reliance on third-party vendors and external connectivity through resilient OT architecture design. - Identify and mitigate third-party security risks across the OT ecosystem. - Apply zero trust and defense-in-depth to secure industrial control systems and operational networks. - Limit third-party attack surfaces using secure remote access, network segmentation, and privileged access controls. - Establish governance and operational frameworks that maintain business continuity during third-party service disruptions.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Vincent Amanyi, Founder | Boleaum Inc.

item.title: Strengthening CNI Continuity Amid Sophisticated Cyber Attacks
item.description:
Critical infrastructure now operates at the intersection of IT and operational technology. As adversaries escalate attacks, outages threaten public safety, economic stability and stakeholder trust. Meanwihle, regulatory scrutiny is rising, making resilience both a board priority and an operational imperative.
Many organizations are struggling to “keep the lights on” while managing so much ICT change across complex, legacy-rich environments. This session examines the current level of threats to Critical National Infrastructure (CNI) and the underlying impacts on society and the economy, exploring practical strategies for continuity of essential services during sophisticated cyber incidents.
Join Steve Yates, Chairman of the Resilience Association and Liveryman of the Worshipful Company of Information Technologists, to explore frontline practices in continuity for ICT and critical infrastructure operators.
Key Takeaways - Map today’s CNI threat landscape and prioritize mission-critical services. - Identify strategic security gaps across ICT/OT, third parties, and change management. - Build incident management that links detection to tested recovery and communications. - Implement safeguards: segmentation, least privilege, offline/immutable backups, and restoration drills. - Establish metrics and exercises to evidence resilience and meet regulatory expectations
item.brighttalk:presenter: Steve Yates, Chairman | Resilience Association

item.title: Reducing Outage Impact: Resilience-by-Design for Critical Services
item.description:
Critical infrastructure now runs on cloud-first services and tightly connected platforms. Disruptions travel quickly across this fabric and when an essential service stumbles, consequences create safety risks, economic loss, regulatory exposure and damage public trust. Adversaries are exploiting ransomware, supply chain compromise, OT/IT convergence and more to accelerate incident speed. In this context, resilience needs to be built in, not bolted on.
Resilience-by-design replaces ad-hoc response by bringing together DevSecOps, cloud-native architecture, SRE, observability, incident response, and disaster recovery to form a measurable, repeatable capability. This session explores strategies for standardizing secure pipelines, automating controls, codifying recovery, and aligning SLOs to business risk. Learn how to map practices to guidance like CISA’s Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goals and NIS2, and use DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) metrics, MTTR, and availability indicators to improve reliability without adding operational drag.
Join Jyotirmayee Pradeep Kumar, Vice President, Cloud DevOps at a global bank, to explore patterns that protect critical services while sustaining availability and continuity. - Embed resilience into architecture and platform design by identifying critical services, dependencies, failure modes and attack surfaces. - Build secure cloud and DevSecOps foundations with standardized CI/CD, automated security testing, vulnerability remediation, and Kubernetes guardrails. - Reduce blast radius and accelerate detection and response using unified. observability, SLI/SLOs, service health metrics, and structured incident response - Recover faster with Infrastructure-as-Code, automated runbooks, tested disaster recovery strategies and resilient multi-region platforms.
Prioritize investments and demonstrate risk reduction by using DORA metrics, MTTR and reliability indicators to measure what really matters
item.brighttalk:presenter: Jyotirmayee Pradeep Kumar, Vice President - CoreDev DevOps | International Banking

item.title: AI Incident Response in Critical Infrastructure: Who Takes Command?
item.description:
What happens when an AI system supporting an essential service produces an unsafe recommendation, is manipulated or fails during a cyber incident? Traditional incident response plans usually say who handles a network intrusion. However, they often do not clarify who can pause an AI system, override its output, check its impact or decide when it can return to service.
In this session, Jennifer Raiford presents an executive approach to AI incident response for critical infrastructure. She explains how to set up a clear chain of command that includes security, operations, AI governance, legal, and executive teams. She also focuses on keeping people in charge of important decisions and rehearsing response before a failure affects the public.
Key takeaways: - Recognize when an AI failure or misuse requires incident escalation. - Assign authority to pause, override, investigate, and restore an AI system. - Coordinate cyber response, operational continuity, and public communication. - Exercise AI incident scenarios before they affect essential services.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Jennifer Raiford, CEO, Globe-Sec Advisory & Defense and CISO & Chief Digital Trust & Risk Officer, Enigma Protocol

item.title: Securing AI Agent Reasoning Against Logic-Layer Attacks in 90 Days
item.description:
Autonomous AI agents are reshaping enterprise operations. Their advanced reasoning can design and execute multi-step, high-privilege workflow actions. This makes the logic layer vulnerable to goal hijacking, indirect prompt injection and unauthorized tool use. As the EU AI Act takes effect and boards require clear accountability, failures at the logic level carry heavy consequences.
Traditional controls can't monitor or validate the complex decision loops of autonomous agents. Enterprises need a deterministic control plane that separates reasoning from execution and verifies intent before actions occur. This control plane should also enforce policies that are testable, auditable, and aligned with NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001 standards.
This session presents actionable architectures that allow CIOs, CISOs, and architects to deploy agentic AI quickly while maintaining oversight.
Join Eugina Jordan, CEO and Co-Founder at YOUnifiedAI, to discover proven blueprints, practical implementation patterns and get a 90-day roadmap for deploying secure, audit-ready AI agents at scale.
Key Takeaways - Pinpoint where to enforce controls across the four-layer stack: Model, Reasoning, Execution, and Enterprise Logic. - Treat agents as managed identities by enforcing least privilege, just-in-time authorization, and API contracts that strictly define tool access. - Defend against advanced threats by applying I/O filtering and provenance controls to counter indirect prompt injection, tool hijacking, and logic-level exploits. - Adopt a reference architecture and measurable metrics to pilot, strengthen, and scale agentic AI deployments with clear audit evidence.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Eugina Jordan, CEO & Co-Founder | YOUnifiedAI

item.title: The Five-Layer Stack Behind Every Defensible AI System
item.description:
Enterprise AI is deciding, detecting, and acting in production, while security and governance are still being retrofitted from procurement checklists and annual audits. This session from industry thought leader Noah M. Kenney introduces the AI Governance Stack, a five-layer operating model spanning data, models, system integration, control and monitoring, and audit and evidence.
Through a case-study walkthrough of a high-risk enterprise AI system, attendees will see how each layer produces controls that support existing cybersecurity functions, satisfy governance and audit requirements from a single source of truth, and make AI systems defensible to regulators, boards, and incident responders.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Noah M. Kenney, Founder & CEO | Digital 520

item.title: Reduce AI Risk with Threat Intelligence–Driven SecOps
item.description:
AI-driven automation is reshaping internal operations, but it is also widening the attack surface. Without a clear grasp of the security risks unique to AI, organizations risk exposing critical assets and undermining trust. Addressing these vulnerabilities early is essential to ensure AI deployments strengthen your security posture.
This session explores approaches for securing AI operations and strengthening threat intelligence. We will focus on establishing effective security controls, maintaining continuous oversight of AI environments, detecting anomalous activity and responding rapidly to new threats.
Join Ernesto Marquez, Project Director at Concurrency Labs Ltd., for actionable guidance on deploying secure AI solutions and building rapid detection and response capabilities within your organization.
Key Takeaways: - Identify key risks and common misconfigurations in AI-driven tools and processes. - Apply targeted prevention strategies and evaluate tools that improve threat detection, visibility, and incident resolution. - Strengthen AI resilience, enhance threat visibility, and adopt proactive security strategies for secure AI application deployment.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Ernesto Marquez, Project Director | Concurrency Labs Ltd

item.title: How to Assess AI Security
item.description:
AI system security is imperative with its large uptick in use. Given the complexities of both AI and security, management requires assurance that systems comply with both corporate policy and external regulations. The challenge lies in how to assess such a rapidly evolving technical environment such as AI.
This presentation offers a framework for assessing security from an AI perspective and AI system development from a security perspective. It then goes deeper, presenting assessment programs for 12 aspects of AI security, including access controls, recoverability, ethics and robustness.
Key Takeaways: - The balance between assessments and audits of AI security. - Basic principles of security, from an AI perspective. - Basic principles of managed AI risk, from a security perspective. - The questions to ask and tests to perform in assessing AI security.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Steven Ross, Executive Principal | Risk Masters International

item.title: Proving Threat Hunting ROI: Outcome-Based KPIs for the Modern SOC
item.description:
Automated tools miss the threats that cause the most damage. While threat hunting is essential for modern security operations, its value is often measured by the number of hunts completed—a metric that overlooks its true operational impact. Without a clear framework for demonstrating risk reduction and guiding detection engineering, SOC leaders struggle to justify investment and prioritize resources.
Security teams must adopt outcome-based measurement to capture the full value of threat hunting. This session outlines a practical approach for evaluating threat hunting with KPIs that matter: hypothesis quality, visibility gaps, adversary techniques addressed, and quantifiable risk reduction. These metrics directly inform improvements in MTTD, MTTR, dwell time, and false negatives. Learn how to translate technical hunting results into executive insights that demonstrate resilience gains and support a proactive SOC strategy.
Join John Bambenek, President of Bambenek Consulting, to discover proven methods for quantifying threat hunting value and securing the resources your team needs to advance.
Key Takeaways: - Define outcome-based KPIs for threat hunting and eliminate vanity metrics. - Connect hunt outcomes to risk posture by tracking MTTD, MTTR, dwell time, and false negative trends to justify investment. - Audit and document hypothesis quality and coverage to improve efficiency. - Present technical results in executive terms, highlighting cost avoidance and strategic roadmap impact.
item.brighttalk:presenter: John Bambenek, President | Bambenek Consulting

item.title: Translate Security Operations Metrics into Business Risk Intelligence
item.description:
Security operations centers produce a lot of data, including alert counts, MTTR, MTTD, incident volumes, and automation rates. But does having all this information really make us safer?
As regulatory pressures and board oversight intensify, security leaders need to be able to translate daily operational work into strategic risk insights that executives actually understand. Without this, CISOs struggle to justify security budgets and demonstrate their value to the business. Traditional SecOps metrics like ticket closure rates and detection speeds only tell part of the story. Modern security leaders need frameworks that connect operational performance to exposure reduction, resilience building and strategic decision-making.
This session will show you how to turn raw security data into risk intelligence that makes sense to executives and boards. We’ll also look at how AI-driven automation is changing what we measure and helping organizations move away from reactive risk management, towards a proactive approach that supports smart investments and shared accountability.
Join Oksana Denesiuk, Board Member for ISSA LA and Senior Product Manager at Kaiser Permanente, to learn practical ways to improve your security operations reporting.
Key Takeaways: - Why traditional SecOps metrics (alert volume, MTTR, MTTD) fail without business context. - Practical frameworks for translating operational security data into risk intelligence that drives prioritization and investment decisions - How AI and automation are transforming next-generation security operations, measurement and resilience strategies. - Proven communication techniques CISOs use to present security performance meaningfully to boards and cross-functional stakeholders. - Actionable methods to align SecOps metrics with exposure reduction, business impact, and organizational resilience goals.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Oksana Denesuik, Senior Production Manager, Solutions Consultant - Billing | Kaiser Permanente

item.title: Implement Data-Driven Security with AI and Visual Intelligence
item.description:
The video surveillance side of the security industry is experiencing its 'iPhone moment.' For more than two decades, physical security ran a predictable playbook. Today, that legacy framework traps organizations in massive "hardware debt" -- consuming storage, energy, space, and hands-on maintenance no one wants -- all while capturing situations and near-misses after it is too late. Advanced cloud architecture and edge-AI are completely eliminating the centralized bottleneck, giving rise to intelligent AI orchestration layers that instantly transform standard cameras into proactive, real-time "video supervisors." Physical security is being rewritten by tools that can deploy custom video-AI agents tracking dwell time, enforcing PPE, collecting business intelligence, and flagging anomalies before harm occurs.
This structural shift has fundamentally flipped corporate expectations on their head. Integrators and security operators are no longer just field technicians; they have been thrust into the role of AI consultants.
The true differentiator for modern security leadership will not be the speed of deployment, but the caliber of data-driven governance. This session from CEO Robert Messer will deliver concrete guidance on how to move beyond legacy security mindsets, establish objective performance metrics that resonate with the C-suite, and confidently navigate the transition from capital-intensive on-premises hardware to secure, provable results in the cloud.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Robert Messer, Founder &CEO | IP TechView

item.title: Optimizing SOC Defense with Emerging Tech for the AI Era
item.description:
Cyber adversaries are moving faster, using automation and AI to overwhelm traditional defenses. Legacy SOC architectures cannot keep pace with the scale and speed of these attacks. As the enterprise attack surface expands, security leaders face a critical challenge: adapt their SOC strategy or risk falling behind. The surge of new tools promises solutions, but the real difficulty lies in pinpointing the technologies that will deliver measurable impact and understanding how to integrate them effectively.
Security leaders require a practical framework for technology selection that cuts through vendor claims and focuses on tools proven to reduce risk. This session examines how to strategically integrate advanced capabilities that align with compliance requirements, fit within complex environments, and support human analysts without adding to alert fatigue.
Join Charles Kolodgy, Principal at Security Mindsets LLC, for guidance on how to modernize your SOC, optimize technology procurement, and build a more resilient, analyst-centered human-machine defense model.
Key Takeaways: - Evaluate the real-world strengths and limitations of AI-driven defensive tools to inform objective procurement decisions. - Align technology investments with your current security frameworks and the maturity of your incident response teams. - Assess how new technologies impact SOC workflows, security frameworks, and operational maturity. - Integrate intelligent automation into SOC workflows to support analysts, reduce burnout, and accelerate detection and response times. - Prepare your SOC infrastructure for next-generation advancements, including agentic AI and proactive defense models.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Charles Kolodgy, Principal | Security Mindsets LLC

item.title: Preparing Security Analysts for the Reality of Modern Security Operations
item.description:
Security analysts need more than just technical skills to handle the realities of modern operations. AI, automation, and expanding attack surfaces have outpaced traditional training and certifications. As threats evolve, organizations face a critical skill gap: analysts need to be ready to make decisions and adapt under pressure, not just execute technical tasks.
Effective analysts do more than investigate alerts. They make informed decisions under pressure, align with business priorities, and collaborate across teams to drive incident response. To develop these capabilities, organizations need to move beyond technical training and intentionally build operational readiness.
Drawing on real-world experience leading enterprise security operations and vulnerability management programs, Mari Galloway shares practical strategies to develop analysts prepared for the moments that matter. Attendees will examine how experiential learning, cross-functional collaboration, leadership development and targeted technology adoption combine to build confident analysts and resilient security teams.
Learning Objectives - Assess how AI and automation are redefining the analyst’s role, shifting focus from technical execution to operational decision-making. - Learn practical strategies to develop operationally-ready analysts through experiential learning, cross-functional collaboration and real-world incident preparedness. - Adopt leadership approaches that strengthen decision-making, communication and operational effectiveness so analysts can navigate complex incidents with confidence. - Create development pathways that improve analyst retention, build organizational resilience and prepare the next generation of security operations professionals.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Mari Galloway, CEO & Founding Board Member | Cyberjutsu

item.title: Automating Evidence and Policy Checks for AIOps
item.description:
AI-driven applications, APIs, autonomous workflows, and digital workers are becoming active participants in business operations. As organizations increasingly rely on non-human actors to make decisions, execute transactions, and access sensitive data, the attack surface extends beyond traditional vendor boundaries.
When trust breaks down—through excessive permissions, model drift, compromised integrations, or unauthorized agent behavior—the consequences can include operational disruption, fraud, compliance failures, and reputational damage. Security operations must evolve from verifying who has access to continuously validating how AI-enabled systems behave and whether their actions align with business intent.
Traditional third-party assessments provide only a point-in-time view of risk. They offer limited visibility into the real-time actions of AI agents, SaaS extensions, and digital workers. As AI adoption accelerates, security teams need continuous, evidence-driven verification of both human and non-human identities.
Join Sandra Estok, Founder and CEO of Way2Protect, to explore a practical approach for extending security operations through continuous verification. Learn how to apply least privilege, implement runtime policy validation, establish accountability across suppliers and internal teams, and enable trusted AI innovation without sacrificing resilience.
Key Takeaways - Understand why AI-enabled workflows challenge traditional third-party risk and supply chain security assumptions. - Learn how to verify identity, authority, behavior, and outcomes across AI agents, digital workers, and interconnected systems. - Apply practical guardrails including least privilege, runtime policy validation, continuous evidence, and human oversight. - Establish clear accountability and escalation paths across suppliers, platforms, and internal teams. - Leave with a practical blueprint for extending security operations to support trusted AI-enabled business ecosystems.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Sandra Estok, Founder & CEO | Way2Protect

item.title: Scaling Operational Resilience Against AI-Driven Threats
item.description:
AI adoption is accelerating business operations, but it is also expanding the attack surface beyond the reach of traditional security models. While this enables speed and agility, it has expanded the attack surface faster than traditional security models can deliver protection.
This session examines how the evolving cybersecurity landscape is both driving progress and introducing new risks. We will outline practical strategies to build resilience and agility into security operations, enabling organizations to manage complexity at scale.
Steve Yates, Resilience Association Chairman and Liveryman of the Worshipful Company of Information Technology (WCIT), will address the real-world challenges organizations face in Security Operations Transformation. He will share actionable strategies for early risk detection, security management and building a resilient operational foundation.
Key Takeaways: - Assess interoperable security models and automation strategies. - Address attack surface fragmentation and close the budget maturity gap. - Identify where operational complexity exceeds current skillsets and outline upskilling priorities for security teams. - Examine executive perspectives on operational priorities amid a shifting threat landscape. - Tackle key cybersecurity threats and operational resilience challenges head-on.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Steve Yates, Chairman | Resilience Association

item.title: Securing AI-Driven Supply Chains Before the Next Breach
item.description:
Supply chains remain one of the most exposed attack surfaces in cybersecurity. Even as organizations invest in internal defenses, they depend on vendors, partners, and service providers with direct access to sensitive data and core systems. This dependence introduces risk at every connection point. When trust is assumed rather than verified, security gaps multiply.
AI adoption is exacerbating this risk. Vendors now use AI to develop products, write code, assess security and automate operations. This leads to unvetted applications, insufficiently reviewed code and security reports that may be more superficial than substantive. Automation can introduce vulnerabilities that even the vendor does not fully grasp. These unknowns escalate the risk that supply chains pose to organizational security.
CISO Alex Holden cuts through compliance checklists and legal jargon to expose the real threats lurking in supply chains. He identifies the missteps that open the door to breaches and offers practical strategies for communicating risk to vendors, partners and customers. Learn how to assess whether your supply chain is truly secure, spot superficial AI-driven security claims and strengthen defenses by collaborating with suppliers rather than relying solely on audits.
Takeaways: - Pinpoint how systems, data, and access are managed and protected throughout your supply chain. - Identify the risks introduced by poorly reviewed AI-assisted development. - Shift from audits to collaboration: communicate risk clearly and validate essential security practices with your suppliers.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Alex Holden, CISSP, Chief Information Security Officer | Hold Security LLC

item.title: Transform SBOM from Compliance Burden to Strategic Security Intelligence
item.description:
With software supply chain attacks on the rise and regulations tightening worldwide, organizations face a critical choice: treat the Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) as yet another box to check or see it as a powerful security tool to transform risk management across the entire enterprise.
Most organizations produce SBOMs simply to meet compliance requirements—creating static documents that are quickly forgotten and never put to use. In this session, you’ll learn how to turn SBOMs from a one-time inventory into a living, organization-wide intelligence system that’s woven into every part of your security ecosystem. We’ll explore how having detailed, component-level insight makes it easier to spot vulnerabilities early, respond to incidents faster and keep risks in check continuously. When SBOM data is integrated into your development and security processes, it lays the groundwork for smarter decision-making that not only protects your critical systems but also keeps your business agile.
Join Vincent Amanyi, Founder of Boleaum Inc., to explore how leading organizations are shifting from reactive compliance to proactive security governance.
Key Takeaways: - See exactly what software components and dependencies you have, along with the risks they bring to your supply chain. - Find and fix known vulnerabilities faster, making your vulnerability management process more efficient. - Improve your governance and compliance with documentation that’s ready for audits and helps you meet regulations and report risks clearly. - Move from just reacting to compliance needs to actively monitoring risks and building a stronger security approach. - Make better strategic decisions by using SBOM workflows that are built into your processes.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Vincent Amanyi, Founder | Boleaum Inc.

item.title: Trusted Supply Chains Start with Verified Data
item.description:
Most supply chain security failures are not caused by a lack of technology but by unverified information moving too freely across organizational boundaries. This session reframes trust as a data problem and explains why the ability to verify who, what, where, and when is becoming central to resilient supply chain operations. It will explore how standardized identification and authoritative data verification can reduce impersonation, counterfeit exposure, and process ambiguity before they become operational incidents.
For executive audiences, the relevance is strategic. Trusted data is the foundation for faster decisions, better automation, and stronger enterprise value protection. We will discuss how supply chain built on data verification supports procurement, logistics, compliance, and AI-enabled operations makes information more portable, more consistent, and more defensible. That shift creates a measurable advantage in resilience, transparency, and board-level confidence. The payoff is not just better security; it is lower fraud risk, fewer onboarding exceptions, cleaner audit trails, and a supply chain that is easier to govern at scale.
Key Takeaways: - Why data verification is now a supply chain security requirement, not a back-office detail. - How authoritative sources reduce impersonation and fraud at key transaction points. - Where standardized data improves AI readiness and operational automation. - How to align resilience, compliance, and commercial performance around trusted data.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Obuks Akpede, Data Governance Consultant | Adastra Corporation

item.title: From Vendors to Digital Workers: Verifying Trust in the Agentic Supply Chain
item.description:
Supply chains are no longer composed only of organizations, software, and service providers. Increasingly, enterprise workflows now depend on AI-enabled systems, autonomous processes, and digital workers operating across supplier environments.
This shift introduces a new challenge for security leaders: traditional supply chain verification models were designed to assess vendors and technology stacks, not systems capable of making decisions, executing workflows, and continuously adapting across organizational boundaries.
As organizations adopt agentic AI across procurement, operations, customer service, and third-party ecosystems, security teams must evolve from verifying static controls to validating trust, authority, behavior, and accountability across interconnected human and AI-driven work.
In this session, Sandra Estok, Founder and CEO of Way2Protect, explores how security leaders can rethink supply chain verification through the lens of the modern workforce. Attendees will learn practical approaches to evaluate AI-enabled suppliers, apply verification principles to digital workers, and strengthen resilience without slowing innovation.
Key Takeaways - Understand how agentic AI changes traditional supply chain trust assumptions. - Learn practical verification approaches for AI-enabled suppliers and digital workers. - Identify governance gaps between supplier security and operational execution. - Apply security culture and trust principles to modern interconnected ecosystems.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Sandra Estok, Founder & CEO | Way2Protect

item.title: Strengthening Supply Chain Resilience in a High-Risk Geopolitical Environment
item.description:
Supply chain vulnerabilities now pose a direct threat to business continuity. A single compromised third party can disrupt your entire digital ecosystem. In this context, identifying which partners are truly critical is critical to operational resilience.
This session uses the World Economic Forum's Global Value Chains framework to pinpoint persistent risks across your supply chain and align your approach with Critical National Infrastructure (CNI) requirements.
Steve Yates, Resilience Association Chairman and Liveryman of the Worshipful Company of Information Technology (WCIT), will address the real-world challenges organizations face in managing supply chain and third-party risk. He will share actionable strategies for early risk detection, dependency assessment and building a resilient operational foundation.
Key Takeaways: - Identify persistent risks in global supply chains and digital ecosystems. - Examine lessons from major cyberattacks that disrupted global infrastructure and impacted entire communities. - Apply proven methods to review supply chains and establish early warning for emerging risks. - Implement third-party security strategies such as continuous monitoring, dependency mapping, and risk-based assessments. - Strengthen your organization's resilience against supply chain disruption.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Steve Yates, Chairman | Resilience Association

item.title: Disaster Recovery Strategies: One Company, Many Technical Environments
item.description:
Disaster recovery planning used to be simple: have an alternative data center in case the primary one fails. These days, organizations may have a residual data center with only a few applications and network connectivity on premises while the rest of their information systems reside with one or more commercial clouds, XaaS vendors, managed service providers and other third parties. Companies must develop recovery strategies for each environment, as well as for combinations of environments -- for example, a cloud service provider outage that incapacitates the SaaS applications hosted by that vendor.
In this webinar you will learn: - A framework for building a disaster recovery plan based on strategies for diverse technical environments. - How to develop recovery strategies from initial damage assessment to return to normal IT operations. - Interfacing the recovery solutions among all environments. - How to test the effectiveness of recovery strategies.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Steven Ross, Executive Principal | Risk Masters International

item.title: Closing the Recovery Gap: Turning Backup Investments into Proven Resilience
item.description:
For most organizations, the challenge has shifted from investing in backups to mastering recovery. Even with advanced tools, immutable storage and defined RTO and RPO targets, most organizations are still unable to demonstrate recovery at production scale. The gap between having backups and executing recovery when it matters is a major risk. When ransomware hits, theoretical metrics and preparedness plans are put to the test. In that moment, the ability to restore operations at scale becomes the definitive measure of readiness.
This session addresses how to close the recovery gap. Drawing on real-world recovery programs, we look at the practical steps that make recovery achievable: coordinating recovery efforts, understanding system dependencies, preparing safe restore environments, handling contamination, and running practice drills to find weak spots before an incident. We also confront the reporting gap, where leadership sees backup metrics that reassure but say little about restore confidence.
Join Obuks Akpede, Data Governance Consultant at Adastra Corporation to explore how leading enterprises are reframing recovery as an engineered capability.
Key Takeaways: - Apply a practical framework to transform backup operations into engineered recovery capability. - Adopt operational disciplines that build restore confidence and eliminate recovery assumptions. - Design rehearsal programs that reveal real failure modes before incidents occur Implement executive reporting models that translate recovery posture into defensible, board-level assurance. - Close the gap between backup investment and production-scale recovery execution with targeted strategies.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Obuks Akpede, Data Governance Consultant | Adastra Corporation

item.title: 10 Common Sense Solutions to App Sec Challenges - AI Not Required
item.description:
The AI hype has swept over all corners of the IT universe, and application security is no exception. There are AI tools to check source code errors as well as AI solutions to speed up the coding process. However, there remains persistent application security problems that evade AI’s capabilities. For instance, understanding why an application's security features fell short of expectations cannot be solved with a few prompts, nor can data privacy issues be addressed by AI tools alone.
In this presentation, industry thought leader Ralph Villanueva will talk about how human workers and intelligence are still a necessary component for a robust application security program.
Key Takeaways: - Ten common app sec issues still best addressed by humans. - Solutions that are both cost-effective and readily actionable. - Help the audience protect their organizations from financial, operational and reputational app sec risks.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Ralph Villanueva, Cybersecurity Compliance Supervisor | Carnival Corporation

item.title: Harmonizing AI Governance and Cybersecurity Operations
item.description:
AI governance and cybersecurity operations are still running on separate tracks in most organizations. Governance lives with legal, privacy, and risk. Security operations live with detection, incident response, and runtime monitoring. That separation was manageable when AI was a procurement question, but it breaks down the moment AI-driven detection, automated threat hunting, and agentic response tools move into production. AI systems are now a security control, a compliance obligation, and an operational risk all at once.
This session is for CISOs and security leaders who need these two disciplines working from the same playbook. We'll cover what it actually looks like to harmonize AI governance with cybersecurity operations. The goal is one integrated operating model, not two parallel programs generating conflicting requirements for the same teams.
Key takeaways: - A practical model for merging AI governance and security operations workflows without doubling overhead. - Decision criteria for where AI autonomy belongs in detection and response versus where human approval is non-negotiable. - Logging and audit requirements that satisfy incident review, regulatory scrutiny, and AI governance obligations in one pass. - A readiness assessment for identifying where your organization's governance and operational security tracks are quietly in conflict.
About the Speaker Noah M. Kenney is Founder & Principal Consultant of Digital 520, a consultancy operationalizing AI governance, security, and privacy. He authored Governing Intelligence: Law, Privacy, Security, and Compliance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (2026), reaching 100,000+ readers. He is Chief Scientist of the Disruptive AI Lab, President of the Ethical Tech Forum, and holds IAPP CIPM and AIGP certifications.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Noah M. Kenney, Founder & CEO | Digital 520

item.title: AI Did It: Who is Liable for AI Failures in Cybersecurity?
item.description:
With the rapid proliferation of AI into every aspect of corporate cybersecurity and cyber-defense, AI-triggered incidents and omissions will become more and more common.
This session from attorney and CEO will explore how the legislation passed on both sides of the Atlantic addressing AI-provoked incidents and failures and emphasizing prevention and risk mitigation from both technical and legal viewpoints. Attendees will learn more about personal liability of cybersecurity executives, cybersecurity insurance, third-party risk management and other hot topics.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Dr. Ilia Kolochenko, CEO (and attorney-at-law) | ImmuniWeb

item.title: From Axios to Trivy: Stopping the Next Ecosystem-Scale Supply Chain Breach
item.description:
Open-source software is now the backbone of application development—and a prime target for nation-state adversaries and automated malware. Recent incidents, including North Korea's Axios npm compromise, the Shai-Hulud worm, and TeamPCP's attacks on Trivy, all exploited common weaknesses: exposed maintainer accounts, unsecured publish tokens, vulnerable transitive dependencies, and gaps in CI/CD pipelines.
AI is accelerating both attack and defense. Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, intended to identify critical vulnerabilities ahead of adversaries, was itself compromised within hours. Threat actors are now using AI to automate the creation of malicious packages and orchestrate advanced social engineering campaigns.
Join Yesenia Yser for a focused discussion on actionable defense strategies: dependency pinning, SLSA attestations and OIDC-based publishing.
Key Takeaways: - Identify recurring attack patterns to speed threat detection. - Examine human trust and account security as core AppSec concerns. - Reduce transitive dependency risk throughout build pipelines. - Implement AI-driven provenance verification for all dependencies. - Establish proactive security by enforcing strong dependency governance.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Yesenia Yser, Founder | Yes2Tech

item.title: Application Security for the New Age: From Reactive to Proactive
item.description:
In today’s hyper-connected digital ecosystem, applications are no longer isolated tools, but gateways to critical data, services, and infrastructure. High-profile incidents caused by a data breach demonstrate that even a single overlooked vulnerability can expose millions of users and disrupt entire sectors. As modern systems evolve toward cloud-native architectures, APIs, and AI-driven services, the attack surface expands faster than traditional defenses can keep up.
This talk highlights why application security must shift from a reactive measure to a proactive design principle. We explore the state of the art in secure development, including DevSecOps, automated vulnerability detection, and zero-trust approaches, while addressing the real-world challenges of complexity, human factors, and supply chain risks. The goal is to motivate a mindset where security is not an afterthought, but an integral part of innovation to ensure that the systems we build are not only functional, but resilient and trustworthy.
Key Takeaways: - Treat security as a design principle, not a patch. - Build secure systems from the start, not after deployment. - Maintain visibility of assets, dependencies, and data flows. - Recognize that most breaches stem from known, unpatched flaws. - Adopt secure coding practices and foster a security-first culture.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Yeghisabet Alaverdyan, Senior Researcher | IIAP MESCSA RA

item.title: Closing the Browser Gap: Defending Against AiTM and Shadow AI
item.description:
The browser represents a critical blind spot in enterprise security. That's because it allows threats like Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) attacks, session hijacking and shadow AI tools to bypass traditional defenses. Even with better email security, endpoint protection, and zero-trust systems, businesses still face more account hacks and data leaks. Why? Because attackers are exploiting browser-layer vulnerabilities that operate within trusted sessions.
This session is designed for security leaders who want to see why current defenses fall short against these threats and what they can actually do about it. Through real-life examples, Yaamini Barathi Mohan, CEO of Secto.io will show how attackers get around MFA, take advantage of SaaS platforms and use shadow AI to expose data without anyone noticing. Attendees will leave with practical ways to add browser security to your zero-trust setup—without slowing anyone down.
Key Takeaways: - Understand why the browser is now a primary attack surface for enterprises. - Learn how session-based attacks bypass MFA and traditional detection. - Discover governance strategies for mitigating shadow AI risks. - Explore practical steps to integrate browser security into a zero-trust architecture. - Prioritize investments to effectively close browser-layer security gaps.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Yaamini Barathi Mohan, CEO | Secto.io

item.title: Red Teaming AI: A CISO's Guide to Proactive Defense
item.description:
With large language models and AI systems moving beyond experimentation and into mission-critical operations, organizations face a new generation of security and governance challenges. Traditional cybersecurity controls are insufficient for AI systems, whose dynamic and often unpredictable nature introduces risks across confidentiality, integrity, availability, safety and trust.
In this session, you'll discover how red teaming has emerged as a practical and essential control for AI risk management. We'll explore how adversarial testing techniques can uncover critical vulnerabilities and provide a structured approach to AI red teaming that aligns with modern governance frameworks and integrates seamlessly into continuous testing throughout your AI lifecycle.
Join Dr. Kellep Charles, Cybersecurity Chair and AI Security and Governance Expert at Capitol Technology University, as he bridges the gap between theory and operational practice—showing you how to make red teaming a core pillar of your AI governance strategy.
Key Takeaways - Understand why traditional security controls fall short for AI systems. - Identify common AI vulnerabilities, including prompt injection and data leakage. - Learn how to implement structured red teaming methodologies for LLMs. - Explore how red teaming aligns with enterprise AI governance frameworks. - Gain practical strategies for integrating continuous AI security testing into your operations.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Kellep Charles, Chair of Cybersecurity Programs & Director of AI Governance | Capitol Technology University

item.title: AI Agents Unleashed: Governing the Invisible Workforce
item.description:
As organizations accelerate adoption of agentic AI, they face a paradox: the tools driving innovation create huge security blind spots. Traditional IAM frameworks and security controls are not built to manage the unique challenges posed by AI agents, which operate autonomously, acquire system-level access and execute actions at machine speed. With 81% of teams deploying AI agents but only 14% securing formal approval, risks escalate rapidly, leaving businesses vulnerable to breaches, compliance failures and operational disruptions.
The AI security paradox is fundamentally an identity governance problem. AI agents bypass traditional provisioning, operate across complex delegation chains and lack the audit trails regulators will soon demand. Addressing this requires a paradigm shift. Platform engineering teams must treat AI agents as a distinct identity class, applying policy-as-code frameworks, dynamic risk-based authorization, and full observability to every agent action. This approach helps businesses mitigate risks without stifling innovation, ensuring AI adoption aligns with security and compliance mandates.
Join Atulpriya Sharma, Principal Developer Advocate at Improving, CNCF Ambassador to uncover actionable strategies for governing AI agents and securing your organization’s future.
Key Takeaways: - Recognize why AI agents represent a new, ungoverned identity class beyond traditional IAM capabilities. - Learn how AI agents silently acquire system-level access and the risks this poses Explore policy-as-code frameworks to govern agent behavior without hindering innovation. - Discover observability techniques to create robust audit trails for regulatory compliance. - Gain a practical governance blueprint to align platform and security teams effectively.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Atulpriya Sharma, Principal Developer Advocate | Improving

item.title: The CISO's Playbook: Turning AI Governance Into Boardroom Currency
item.description:
AI governance talks often stop at risk mitigation. But for security leaders who are already beyond the basics, a bigger question looms: will governance slow your organization down, or can it become your competitive edge? Forward-looking CISOs are flipping the script by treating AI governance as a strategic business capability rather than a compliance checkbox. This gives them more influence in the boardroom, stronger leverage in procurement, and greater credibility across the enterprise.
For governance to stick and scale, it must be owned across legal, product, data science and procurement—but cross-functional buy-in only happens when governance delivers clear strategic value. In this session, you'll discover three ways to make that case: how governance can become a market asset for building trust, turn alliances into an early warning system for AI risks, and craft a boardroom narrative that shifts from controls to capability.
Oksana Denesiuk (Board Member for ISSA LA, Senior Product Manager, Solution Consultant – Billing at Kaiser Permanente) to receive a practical playbook for your board conversation, including specific language shifts that will reframe governance and a blueprint for sharing governance responsibilities across teams. You'll leave with a sharper, more compelling way to translate security work into language that resonates with CEOs and audit committees.
Key Takeaways: - A three-part model for turning AI governance into a competitive and market advantage. - A cross-team strategy that makes governance a shared responsibility across the business, not just in security - Ways to talk about AI risk that show it as a business strength and a way to stand out in procurement. - Metrics that matter to executives: AI governance coverage, speed to safe deployment and how ready you are for regulations compared to others in your industry.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Oksana Denesuik, Board Member for ISSA LA, Senior Product Manager, Solution Consultant – Billing | Kaiser Permanente

item.title: From Tools to Teammates: Governing AI Agents as Enterprise Workers
item.description:
AI agents are rapidly expanding the enterprise attack surface. Unlike human users, these systems execute privileged workflows and make autonomous decisions at a scale and speed that outpace traditional security controls. Existing awareness programs focus on human error, leaving organizations exposed to risks introduced by AI-driven operations.
This session examines where human and AI-driven risks intersect, and why conventional security programs fail to address the unique challenges of autonomous AI workflows. We will outline practical governance strategies to align both human and AI actions with business resilience goals.
Join Sandra Estok, Founder and CEO of Way2Protect, for actionable frameworks to manage the evolving risks of AI in the enterprise.
Key Takeaways: - Pinpoint how agentic AI increases enterprise attack surfaces. - Expose gaps in current security programs for autonomous AI behaviors. - Implement governance that aligns human and AI actions with business objectives. - Develop executive-level communication strategies for AI-driven workforce risks.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Sandra Estok, Founder & CEO | Way2Protect

item.title: Fire, Brimstone and Bad Security Decisions
item.description:
An important facet of resilience in cybersecurity has to do with recovery from making wrong decisions, such as a strategic choice in policy, design, architecture, or even procurement.
How do you back out of something that seemed like a good idea at the time, but that you now realize is creating problems? And how can we stay curious in the face of being wrong, as well as design security for the future to make redirection easier?
This session covers the need to plan for human fallibility – and may itself be wrong …
item.brighttalk:presenter: Wendy Nather, Advisor | EPSD

item.title: Mitigating AI Risks: Understanding and Addressing the Risks of AI Systems
item.description:
AI systems differ from traditional IT systems. Additionally, they are more complex and dynamic, which makes their risks harder to predict and manage. These systems introduce unique challenges, like operational unpredictability, sensitivity to environmental changes, functional error and uncertainty, and new forms of cyber threats. These risks can impact reliability, scalability and overall business performance, making it essential for organizations to address them effectively.
This session will break down the distinct risks of AI systems and explore practical strategies businesses can use to mitigate them. By addressing these challenges, organizations can better protect their AI systems and ensure they operate with sufficient reliability while supporting long-term growth and innovation.
Join Allan Cytryn, Principal at Risk Masters International, to explore effective strategies for managing AI risks and ensuring the resilience of your organization.
Key Takeaways: - Understand why AI risks are more complex than traditional IT risks. - Learn about the unique vulnerabilities of AI systems. - Discover emerging strategies for managing AI risks effectively. - Gain insights into building reliable and scalable AI systems.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Allan Cytryn, Principal | Risk Masters International

item.title: Learning from Mistakes: Hard Lessons in Building Cyber Defenses
item.description:
Most security architectures are built around vendor guidance, compliance frameworks and assumed best practices. But real attackers don’t follow these models. Adversaries are adapting faster than most defensive programs, exploiting predictable gaps and repeated design mistakes. The stakes are high, and organizations need to rethink their approach to stay ahead.
This session focuses on building cyber defenses grounded in real-world attack patterns rather than theoretical frameworks. Drawing from direct observations of threat actor behavior, we’ll explore where defensive architectures fail, why these failures persist and how they are leveraged in modern intrusions. Attendees will gain practical guidance to align defenses with how attacks actually happen, addressing challenges like AI-driven threats, criminal ecosystems and the impact of human error.
Join Alex Holden, CISSP, Chief Information Security Officer at Hold Security, LLC, to learn how to fortify your defenses against today’s most sophisticated threats.
Key Takeaways: - Identify and eliminate repeatable failure points in security architectures. - Design defenses based on real-world attack paths, not theoretical frameworks - Adapt continuously to evolving threats, including AI-driven attacks. - Mitigate the impact of human error on otherwise well-designed systems.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Alex Holden, Chief Information Security Officer | Hold Security LLC

item.title: Driving Security Culture Evolution for Business Growth
item.description:
Modern businesses face a critical challenge: balancing innovation with robust security practices. For years, security teams have been perceived as barriers to progress, enforcing controls that slow operations. However, the evolving threat landscape demands a shift in perspective—security must transform into a strategic enabler of growth, resilience and trust.
This session explores how security leaders can redefine their role, moving from reactive gatekeepers to proactive growth partners. Mari Galloway, CEO and Founding Board Member of Cyberjutsu, shares actionable insights from real-world transformations, including a groundbreaking initiative that resolved over one million vulnerabilities. Attendees will gain a practical framework for fostering collaboration, enhancing communication and embedding security into the fabric of organizational culture.
Join Mari Galloway to discover how intentional leadership can position security as a cornerstone of innovation and operational success.
Takeaways:
- Understand the business impact of a collaborative security culture - Learn strategies to align security with organizational goals - Explore real-world examples of successful security transformations - Gain a framework for driving cultural change and building trust - Discover leadership techniques to elevate security’s role in innovation
item.brighttalk:presenter: Mari Galloway, CEO, Founding Board Member | Cyberjutsu

item.title: Synthetic Risk, Authentic Trust: Enterprise Security in the Age of AI
item.description:
We've entered a new era where identities can be fabricated in moments, AI can convincingly impersonate senior leaders and synthetic activity can silently penetrate our most trusted systems. In this evolving environment, resilience is no longer just defined by firewalls, patch management or perimeter security. Now it’s measured by how trust is systematically engineered and embedded into the very foundation of the enterprise.
In this session, Jennifer Raiford widely recognized as The Olivia Pope of Cyber & AI redefines security architecture for a reality where truth can be replicated and visibility is essential for survival.
Drawing on her extensive experience, Jennifer highlights how even with advanced technology, many organizations remain at risk because their designs lack a strong identity foundation. She explains why established security models struggle keeping pace with synthetic threats, how AI-powered impersonation is changing the risk landscape, and why building true resilience requires leaders to start thinking beyond technology, drawing on skills in strategy, diplomacy and design.
This session offers a clear, actionable plan for CISOs and enterprise leaders to build stronger security, centered on identity, smart AI defenses and systems that are ready for today’s fast-changing threats. You’ll walk away with practical tools to design security architectures that can keep up with new threats and safeguard your organization’s integrity even as deepfakes and synthetic identities become more commonplace.
Key Takeaways - Why identity is now the primary control plane for resilience. - How AI‑driven impersonation and synthetic activity reshape architectural risk. - A new approach to resilience: build security around trust, intelligent systems and strong identity controls. - Architectural patterns that withstand manipulation, misinformation and machine‑speed threats. - Leadership behaviors that create clarity, visibility and resilience across the enterprise.
item.brighttalk:presenter: Jennifer Raiford, CEO & Chief Information Security Officer | Globe-Sec Advisory

item.title: Closing the Resilience Gap: Security Architecture for Modern Threats
item.description:
CISOs face converging risks, including AI-driven cyberattacks, geopolitical instability and threats to critical infrastructure. These factors make architectural resilience essential for business continuity and national security. The World Economic Forum’s Global Cybersecurity Outlook reports that 72% of organizations have seen increased cyber risk. Consequently, governments are preparing for inevitable disruptions to critical national infrastructure.
This session identifies structural gaps that increase organizational vulnerability and explores how CISOs can strengthen security architecture to address evolving threats. You will gain practical strategies for managing third-party risks, implementing Minimum Viable Security frameworks, navigating AI governance, and achieving regulatory compliance across jurisdictions, while maintaining operational agility in a dynamic environment.
Join Steve Yates, Resilience Association Chairman and Liveryman of the Worshipful Company of Information Technology (WCIT), as he discusses current challenges for CISOs. He will share strategies to stay ahead of cybersecurity threats and outline ways to strengthen organizational cyber resilience.
